name: Morrígan, Battle-Crow Fate Queen
loreTies: Morrígan embodies battle-crow fate, war prophecy, sovereignty, and doom omens within Avalora.
The Silver-Root Gate allows this deity to enter Ascension-era dungeon routes without collapsing the individuality of other Realms.
Tuatha culture, symbols, weapons, and divine law shape every ability, artifact, silhouette, and combat choice.
shortBackstory: Morrígan, Battle-Crow Fate Queen, is a playable goddess in Mythos Gates: Ascension. Morrígan is the true source-realm divinity behind the mythology — battle-crow fate, war prophecy, sovereignty, and doom omens. Ascension expands divine power during the current Gate crisis; it does not turn a mortal into a god.

chapters.title: Divine Origin
chapters.text: Morrígan is not a mortal hero inspired by myth. Morrígan is the actual goddess recognized by Tuatha source culture, born from the supernatural laws of Avalora. Their domain — battle-crow fate, war prophecy, sovereignty, and doom omens — determines their symbols, weapons, posture, combat instincts, and relationship to sacred authority.

chapters.title: Faction Bond
chapters.text: Within Tuatha, Morrígan expresses the civilization rather than merely representing it. Their visual identity must carry the materials, beauty standards, divine symbols, and sacred rules of Avalora. Their gameplay role, Breaker, must grow from mythology first and mechanics second.

chapters.title: Mythos Gate Wound
chapters.text: During the Ascension era, Morrígan can interact with The Silver-Root Gate because divine beings are intrinsically connected to their Realms. The Gate does not become a simple teleportation portal; it is a mysterious boundary where separate mythological realities become traversable. Morrígan understands some rites of crossing, but not the complete origin of the Mythos Gates.

chapters.title: Dungeon Role
chapters.text: When selected by the player, Morrígan enters the dungeon alone as one god or goddess against multiple enemies. No army follows. No squad shares control. Every room, trap, shrine, relic, elite, and boss encounter must test how battle-crow fate, war prophecy, sovereignty, and doom omens survives pressure from creatures, rival Realm laws, and unstable Gate conditions.

chapters.title: Ascension Conflict
chapters.text: Ascension is the current story arc, not the permanent end-state of the Mythos Gates universe. For Morrígan, Ascension means restoration, awakening, evolution, or expansion of existing divine power. Their personal conflict is to recover strength without reducing Tuatha mythology into raw fuel for the crisis.

relationshipHooks: Faction witnesses interpret how Morrígan crosses The Silver-Root Gate.
Rival deities challenge the limits of cross-Realm travel.
Dungeon lore pickups reveal Gate mystery without resolving the full origin.
developmentStatus: Playable deity backstory aligned to Mythos Gates identity, one-deity dungeon runs, current Ascension arc, and preserved Lore Codex canon.
mythicSource: source culture humans later copied as Celtic and Irish fae myth
visualCanon: Maeve is Avalora’s root-memory voice. Her silver-branch regalia, thorn records, moss-veiled cloak, crow omen marks, and calm dangerous beauty should feel like the origin behind later fae queens and druid archives.

mythosGatesCanon.arcRule: Ascension restores, awakens, evolves, or expands existing divine power; it does not make the character a god for the first time.
